elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may conduct an audit “no more than once in any 12-month period.”

elements.element: Audits require at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “at least 30 days' prior written notice to Licensee.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: The clause states that audits “shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Although the first sentence contemplates an independent CPA or other audit professional, the new sentence affirmatively states that “Licensor may conduct such an audit,” creating ambiguity as to whether Licensor itself may conduct the audit rather than acting solely through the independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause requires that “the auditor shall be bound by written confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is found.
elements.evidence: The cost shift is triggered by any “discrepancy” exceeding 5%, not specifically an underpayment exceeding 5%. This could shift costs for other kinds of discrepancies.

elements.element: Neither Vendor nor the auditor may have direct access to Customer's systems.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “neither Licensor nor the auditor shall have direct access to Licensee's systems.”

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The limit of one audit in any 12-month period is at least as protective as a once-per-year limitation.

elements.element: Audits require at least 15 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless an underpayment exceeding 10% is found.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon any discrepancy exceeding 5%, rather than only upon an underpayment exceeding 10%.

result.reason: Neither level is fully satisfied because the cost-shifting trigger remains materially broader and lower than required. The preferred position also is not cleanly met because “Licensor may conduct” conflicts with the requirement that the audit be conducted by an independent auditor. The redline is not minimal: it adds an unnecessary off-site requirement while failing to correct the cost trigger. The introduced ambiguity over who may conduct the audit also prevents a finding that the drafting preserves intent without contradiction.
